subject: Decision Making
subcategory: The Science of Risk and Reward
title: The Endowment Effect
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Endowment Effect.

hook.text: Give someone a coffee mug and ask them to sell it. They demand twice what buyers will pay. Owning it changed its value.

buildup.text: The Endowment Effect sets up the tradeoffs, the uncertainty, and the decision pressure.

discovery.text: The endowment effect is loss aversion applied to ownership. Selling feels like losing something you have.

twist.text: Experienced traders show less endowment effect. Practice can reduce the bias, but it never disappears completely.

climax.text: The endowment effect inflates what we demand to part with things. We overvalue what we own simply because we own it.

punchline.text: Own it and it is precious. Lose it and it is just a mug.

quiz.question: What causes the endowment effect?
options: Items increase in quality when owned
Loss aversion makes parting with owned items feel like a loss, inflating their perceived value
